Bhoomi

A game where children learn India's traditional land units.

Team
Raj Sonar
Vedant Khedekar
Anurag Joseph
Ashish Asari
Guides
Dr. Mamta N Rao
Prof. Athul Dinesh
Duration
2 weeks
Made for
Param Science Museum, Bengaluru
The challenge

Every region measures land
in their own way.

One acre

12345678

Each block is one kanal. In much of Punjab, eight of them make an acre.

A bigha in one state is not a bigha in the next. Kanal, kattha, cent and biswa also describe land, and each one changes from region to region.

The units are linked, though. In much of Punjab, eight kanal make one acre, so a small plot can be read as a large one once you know the pattern.

Children rarely meet these units in class. So we made a game where they lay out a plot, grow crops on it and find out how much land they have made.

The opportunity

What if children could build a unit of land instead of memorising it?

Conventional learning

Understanding through definitions and numbers.

Experiential learning

Understanding through touch and visual feedback.

We wanted cultural knowledge that children can touch, explore and understand.

The concept

A game built around the land itself.

Bhoomi is a tangible game that connects physical pieces on a board with a digital farm.

A child explores a region, finds its land unit, lays out tiles and grows crops. By the end, the size of the land is something they have built themselves.

Physical play, game-based learning and local storytelling sit on the same board.

Game guide

Meet Bijju, the guide who walks children through the land.

Bijju is the farmer who leads children through the game, from finding their region's land unit to seeing the harvest.

A unit only sticks once a child has handled it. A child who has laid out a bigha with their own hands remembers it longer than one who has read the number in a book.

The interaction

From physical action to digital discovery.

  1. 1

    Explore

    Pick a region and find its traditional land unit.

  2. 2

    Construct

    Place land tiles to build the area you need.

  3. 3

    Cultivate

    Place crops on the land and watch them grow.

  4. 4

    Discover

    See the harvest and compare the land to familiar quantities.

The prototype

Test the experience before building the system.

A working tangible interface would have taken a lot of technical effort. So we used the Wizard of Oz method and simulated the interaction by hand. That left more time to test ideas with users.

Ideate

We explored the interaction, the game mechanics and the possible digital responses.

Simulate

We used the prototype and hand-run responses to stand in for the intended system.

Evaluate

We showed the concept to users and watched how they used it.

Video

The Wizard of Oz test in action

A short clip of a tile being placed, the digital response, a crop growing and the harvest.

Recorded during user testing. The digital responses were run by hand.

The outcome

Making cultural knowledge experiential.

Bhoomi shows how tangible interaction can make India's land measurement systems easier for young learners to reach.

Physical handling, digital storytelling and game mechanics turn an abstract unit into something children can build, see and relate to.
